title: Regularity and well-posedness of the KL-regularized stochastic control problem for fine-tuning diffusion models
author: Yinbin Han, Meisam Razaviyayn, Renyuan Xu
work: Stochastic Control for Fine-tuning Diffusion Models: Optimality, Regularity, and Convergence
source_version: arXiv:2412.18164v4 (CC BY 4.0); Forty-Second International Conference on Machine Learning 2025
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is not obtained by quoting a textbook well-posedness result. Supplying the two smoothness assumptions and the recursive constants of the theory still leaves a source-local backward induction that has to be carried out step by step: the author must first show that the one-step Bellman mapping is strongly concave with the explicit modulus gamma_t built from beta_t, sigma_t and the next-step gradient-Lipschitz constant, obtain the unique optimal control as the fixed point of the implicit relation (20), and then bound the Lipschitz constant of that control by a self-referential inequality that has to be closed using the choice of beta_t. Differentiability of the control is obtained from the smoothing effect of the Gaussian noise through the integration-by-parts formula for the Gaussian density, applied to the derivative of the conditional expectation of the gradient of the value function, and the Lipschitz property of that derivative is then extracted from the same identity; only after the control has been shown to be Lipschitz, differentiable and gradient Lipschitz can the regularity of the value function itself be propagated one step backwards. Closing the induction over all T steps with the four recursively defined constants is a research-level argument in stochastic control, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
